q: We are all walking each other home.
The greatest thing you will ever learn is just to love and be loved in return.
I have found the paradox, that if you love until it hurts, there can be no more hurt, only more love.
There are no goodbyes for us. Wherever you are, you will always be in my heart.

To live in this world, you must be able to do three things: to love what is mortal; to hold it against your bones knowing your own life depends on it; and, when the time comes to let it go, to let it go.
Every man's life ends the same way. It is only the details of how he lived and how he died that distinguish one man from another.
What we have once enjoyed deeply we can never lose. All that we love deeply becomes a part of us.
The bitterest tears shed over graves are for words left unsaid and deeds left undone.
Love is how you stay alive, even after you are gone.
A coward dies a thousand times before his death, but the valiant taste of death but once.
No one is actually dead until the ripples they cause in the world die away.
Unable are the loved to die, for love is immortality.
The song is ended, but the melody lingers on.
We are cups, constantly and quietly being filled. The trick is knowing how to tip ourselves over and let the beautiful stuff out.
As long as there is love and memory, there is no true loss.
The best thing to hold onto in life is each other.
If I had a flower for every time I thought of you, I could walk through my garden forever.
The reality is that you will grieve forever. You will not get over the loss of a loved one; you will learn to live with it.
Tell your friend that in his death, a part of you dies and goes with him. Wherever he goes, you also go.
The cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it, immediately or in the long run.
Conversation enriches the understanding, but solitude is the school of genius.
Only thoughts reached by walking have value.
My argument is not anti-technology, it is pro-conversation.
Simply put, humans are not wired to be constantly wired.
There is a very real zero-sum relationship between online and offline interaction. The moment you are on social media is the moment you are not really engaging with those around you.
The screen replaces the horizon, and in doing so, it shrinks our world.
Every notification is a tiny interruption of your own life story.
You cannot expect an app dreamed up in a dorm room to successfully replace the types of rich interactions to which we have painstakingly adapted over millennia.
Look around you. There is a beautifully complex, uncurated world happening right now.
To be truly present is the ultimate rebellion in an age of distraction.
Leave your phone behind and go outside. Notice how the world does not end, but your mind finally breathes.
We measure our lives in likes instead of laughs, in followers instead of friends.
Turn off the screen and suddenly you are forced to face the silence of your own mind. That is where growth happens.
A digital detox is not a retreat from the world, it is a return to it.
The most important moments in life do not come with a push notification.
Unplugging for a day gives you back a week of mental clarity.
We shape our tools, and thereafter our tools shape us.
Technology is a useful servant but a dangerous master.
Acknowledging the good that you already have in your life is the foundation for all abundance.
I looked around at my life and realized that everything I had ever wanted was already right here.
Gratitude is a divine emotion: it fills the heart, but not to bursting; it warms it, but not to fever.
Walk as if you are kissing the Earth with your feet.
If the only prayer you said was thank you, that would be enough.
Let us rise up and be thankful, for if we didn't learn a lot today, at least we learned a little.
Gratitude changes the pangs of memory into a tranquil joy.
There is always, always, always something to be thankful for.
The real gift of gratitude is that the more grateful you are, the more present you become.
To speak gratitude is courteous and pleasant, to enact gratitude is generous and noble, but to live gratitude is to touch Heaven.
Joy is the simplest form of gratitude.
Gratitude is not only the greatest of virtues, but the parent of all others.
Every joy is gain, and gain is gain, however small.
As we express our gratitude, we must never forget that the highest appreciation is not to utter words, but to live by them.
Find the good. It is all around you.
Some people grumble that roses have thorns; I am grateful that thorns have roses.
Thankfulness is the beginning of gratitude. Gratitude is the completion of thankfulness.
Appreciation is a wonderful thing: it makes what is excellent in others belong to us as well.
The big question about how people behave is whether they have got an Inner Scorecard or an Outer Scorecard. It helps if you can be satisfied with an Inner Scorecard.
No one can construct for you the bridge upon which precisely you must cross the stream of life, no one but you yourself alone.
To find yourself, think for yourself.
If you are always trying to be normal, you will never know how amazing you can be.
I will not let anyone walk through my mind with their dirty feet.
He who depends on himself will attain the greatest happiness.
Your time is limited, so do not waste it living someone else's life.
Do not let the noise of others' opinions drown out your own inner voice.
I care for myself. The more solitary, the more friendless, the more unsustained I am, the more I will respect myself.
You alone are enough. You have nothing to prove to anybody.
Nothing can bring you peace but yourself.
People who want the most approval get the least and the people who need approval the least get the most.
The greatest thing in the world is to know how to belong to oneself.
Freedom is what you do with what's been done to you.
I am the one that has to die when it is time for me to die, so let me live my life the way I want to.
Seek not the good in external things; seek it in yourselves.
Mastering others is strength. Mastering yourself is true power.

It is easy in the world to live after the world's opinion; it is easy in solitude to live after our own; but the great man is he who in the midst of the crowd keeps with perfect sweetness the independence of solitude.
A person who is self-reliant cannot be a victim.
